learning: If s-bend max_error falls below 0.05 m and the oval holds at 1.00, lower mass is the working lever. If oval finish falls or s-bend steering_oscillation exceeds about 0.43, mass has passed its useful range and 0.45 kg is the best tested value.
notes: Iteration 10 geometry and controller unchanged except mass 0.45 to 0.40 kg, the contract minimum, so the race isolates the mass change.
rationale: Iteration 10 (mass 0.45 kg) is the best design so far at 556.7. Its oval finish was 1.00 with max_error 0.021 m, and its s-bend finish was 0.55 with max_error 0.050 m. Mass has been the only lever that has consistently helped the s-bend since iteration 5, and s-bend steering oscillation was 0.36 at 0.45 kg, under the 0.38 threshold. Following the Builder's intent, I keep the iteration 10 geometry and controller exactly, and change only mass to the contract minimum of 0.40 kg. Lower yaw inertia (mass*(L^2+W^2)/12) should cut the remaining off-track exits on the s-bend. Because mass is the only change, any difference from iteration 10 comes from mass alone. I keep kp 3.5, kd 0.6, ki 0.2, base_speed 1.4 and last_direction line loss, since the Builder's evidence does not call for gain changes and the contract physics give no reason to retune the controller for a 0.05 kg change. Prediction, not measurement: s-bend finish rate above 0.55, s-bend max_error at or below 0.05 m, oval finish held at 1.00, and total score above 556.7. Main risk: slip or jitter at the lowest mass, which the observation request will expose through steering_oscillation and max_error.
